title: Dhammapada Verses
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.
groupSub: Reflecting upon and Examining the Dhamma

paras.en:
Mind precedes all actions,
mind is their leader, they are made by mind.
If a person speaks or acts with an impure mind,
dukkha follows them,
like the wheel of a cart follows the foot of the ox.

Mind precedes all actions,
mind is their leader, they are made by mind.
If a person speaks or acts with a pure mind,
happiness follows them,
like a shadow that never leaves.

Good is the taming of the mind,
swift and so hard to control;
going wherever it likes.
A tamed mind brings happiness.

Let the wise one guard the mind,
so difficult to see and very subtle;
going wherever it likes.
A guarded mind brings happiness.

Whatever [harm] an enemy may do to an enemy,
or a hater to a hater,
a mind directed wrongly
can do worse to oneself than that.

Whatever [good] a mother, a father,
or any other relative may do for one,
a mind directed rightly
can do one more good than that.

The bhikkhu who enjoys the Dhamma,
delights in the Dhamma, reflects on the Dhamma,
and recollects the Dhamma —
he does not fall away from the true Dhamma.
